description: SUMMA is the hydrological modelling system developed by Martyn Clark and collaborators for comparing alternative physical formulations. It uses common conservation equations and a numerical solver while varying flux parameterisations, spatial configurations and process choices. Inputs are configured hydrologic response units or nested grids, environmental forcing and model parameters; outputs describe simulated water and energy states and fluxes. Geographic coverage is configurable across catchments and hydroclimatic regimes. Public source is free under GPL-3.0. A limitation is that controlled model comparisons still require appropriate forcing, parameters and numerical choices, and the linked documentation explicitly remains a work in progress. Reproducing another model's behaviour does not independently validate either formulation. SUMMA can examine uncertainty in catchment inflows used for reservoir and flood-infrastructure simulations, complementary to Delft3D FM (model-delft3d-fm). Its README identifies the 2015 concept and implementation papers and the 2021 numerical discussion. No catchment data or model archive was downloaded.
